column1: # The live lane's expected outcomes. Measured 2026-08-31, not estimated.
# EXPECTED EXIT, not "zero". Two of these probes are SUPPOSED to fail right now because they
# reproduce a defect that is filed and unfixed. A lane that demanded exit 0 would be red on
# arrival, and a lane that is always red gets muted -- which is how the recorded baselines in
# the verification skill drifted in the first place (`15/15` was never right, and the admin
# sweep's `GET OK=16 POST OK=4 HTTP503=15` accounts for 35 of 53 discovered routes).
# DRIFT IN EITHER DIRECTION IS A FINDING:
#   expected 1, got 0  -> the defect was fixed. Good. Update this file DELIBERATELY, in the
#                         commit that fixed it, and say so.
#   expected 0, got 1  -> a regression against a real service.
# probe<TAB>expected_exit<TAB>why this is the expected value

column3: The memory lifecycle against a real gateway: supersession, history retained, profile shows current truth only, compaction context carries the new fact and omits the stale one. 14 check() calls — NOT 15, which the skill recorded from the day it was written and which was never true at any revision.
T0-5 is fixed by 29624cb. Both construction paths attribute their writes to Postgres with SQLite at 0 rows. Expected 1 for anyone running origin/main, where the fix is not yet present.
T0-7 fixed 2026-08-31: all four tamper kinds (MODIFY/DELETE/INSERT/LEDGER) detected on BOTH engines. Was exit 1 with three UNDETECTED on Postgres.

CORRECT FAILURE. T0-2 reproduces: a tenant credential sealed on Postgres is unreadable by a fresh process (arm B) or a second replica (arm C), while status still reports it CONFIGURED. Arm D confirms the fail-closed guard holds. This goes to 0 when #123 ships a durable key manager — and that is the exit criterion for #123.

All 53 admin routes against a REAL memotron-admin-server on a fresh graph: OK=21 HTTP400=13 HTTP204=1 HTTP503=18. The 18 are every /api/platform/* route and ALL of them (T1b-9: handler.platform is None in the standalone server and no CLI flag sets it) -- that is the number that moves when the platform surface is wired or removed. The 13 x HTTP400 are correct input validation, verified by reading every message. This REPLACES the prose baseline 'GET OK=16 POST OK=4 HTTP503=15', which accounted for only 35 of 53 because those three buckets do not span the outcome space -- HTTP400 and HTTP204 had no bucket, so 14 outcomes were uncountable. The 'missing 18' was an artifact of the tally, not 18 unexercised routes (#140).

MEASURED 2026-09-11 against DEPLOYED latest, post-merge of #264 -- not a local container this time. exit 0, CONTROL OK with 39 tools enumerated, governance EMPTY=6 ERROR=16 OK=14 SKIP=3. ERROR and SKIP match the pre-migration baseline exactly; the 2 tools that moved OK->EMPTY are a STORE-CONTENT difference (EMPTY means returned nothing) between the dogfood store the old number came from and latest's real one, not a code difference. REQUIRES TWO THINGS, and it exits non-zero without either: a key (MEMOTRON_PROBE_KEY or LITELLM_API_KEY) because latest runs requireGatewayIdentity, and SWEEP_TENANT set to a tenant that key is bound to. Without the key: CONTROL FAIL, exit 2. With the key but the stale default tenant: 36 ERRORs reading `scope 'tenant:memotron-dogfood' is not one of principal 'p-j...'` and exit 1 -- that is the authorization guard working, surfaced as ONE server-level failure rather than 36 tool defects. Both measured on 2026-09-11 before the fix that made them configurable.

MEASURED 2026-09-11 against DEPLOYED latest on FastMCP 4, post-#264: ALL EIGHT ARMS PASS, exit 0. P0 guard armed; A1/A2 each principal writes its own scope; A3 alpha naming bravo's tenant REFUSED (`scope 'tenant:probe-tenant-bravo' is not one of principal 'p-dw-probe-alpha-2''s allowed scopes`); A4 bravo's scope unchanged -- the refusal message is a string the server chose to print, the ABSENT WRITE is the fact; A5 no key 401; A6 /health 200 with no credential; A7 bogus key 401. This row previously read 'EXPECTED, NOT YET MEASURED' because resolve_gateway_identity() calls the gateway admin plane and cannot run locally -- it is now measured and that caveat is retired. REQUIRES two keys bound to DIFFERENT tenants; aliases dw-probe-alpha-2 / dw-probe-bravo-2 expire 2026-09-14T03:58Z. Exits 2 BY DESIGN against a target where MEMOTRON_REQUIRE_GATEWAY_IDENTITY is unset (P0 aborts rather than measuring an unguarded server) and exits 2 if a positive control fails, so a 2 means wrong target or unbound keys, NOT a regression. Leaves probe rows behind by design.
